question:
You are provided with the following:
Solution A containing $2.45\text{ g dm}^{-3}$ of tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid in $250\text{ cm}^3$ of solution.
Solution B containing $1.43\text{ g dm}^{-3}$ of hydrated sodium trioxocarbonate(IV), $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}$ in $100\text{ cm}^3$ of solution.
Methyl orange indicator.

a) Procedure
i) Pipette 20 or $25\text{ cm}^3$ of solution B in to a conical flask. Add 2 drops of methyl orange indicator. Titrate with solution A, from the burette to an orange end point.
ii) Repeat the titration using fresh portions of solution B twice or more. (16 marks)
iii) Find the average titre value. (2 marks)
iv) Write the equation of the reaction. (2 marks)

b) From your results, calculate the:
i) mass concentration $(\text{g dm}^{-3})$ of solution A; (2 marks)
ii) molar concentration of solution A; (4 marks)
iii) amount (moles) of tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid titrated; (4 marks)
iv) amount (moles) of sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) consumed in the reaction; (2 marks)
v) molar concentration of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}$; (3 marks)
vi) relative molar mass of $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}$; (5 marks)
vii) value of $x$ in $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}$. (6 marks)

c) Explain the choice of methyl orange indicator instead of phenolphthalein in the above titration (4 marks)

Carry out the following test and record your observations and inferences clearly, using the normal laboratory format. Credit will be given for Careful Observations clearly recorded and Explanatory Note to account for observed reactions.

A1. You are provided with sample A1 - Lead trioxonitrate(V).
(a) Carry out two (2) confirmatory tests for the cation
(b) Carry out two (2) distinguishing tests for the anion

A2. You are provided with sample A2 - Acetophenone.
a) Record the physical characteristics of the sample.
b) Solubility test: with small quantities of the sample in separate test tubes, determine the solubility of the sample in:
i. water
ii. dilute hydrochloric acid
iii. dilute sodium hydroxide
c) Functional group test:
i. using a cleaned spatula, heat a small quantity of the sample in a Bunsen Burner flame.
ii. to a small quantity of the sample dissolved in ethanol, add small amount of $\text{NaHCO}_3$, warm the resulting mixture and note any gas evolution. If gas is evolved, test its reaction with lime water.
iii. to a small quantity of the sample, add $1\text{ ml}$ of dilute $\text{HCl}$. Heat to boiling, cool and add $1\text{ ml}$ of $2,4$-dinitrophenylhydrazine solution. Allow the solution to stand for 2 minutes.
iv. to a freshly prepared solution of sodium nitroprusside, add small quantity of the sample and then add dilute $\text{NaOH}$ solution drop by drop.
